title: Wiring Regulations (18th Edition)
subtitle: Twenty-two Wiring Regulations practice mocks
description: Twenty-two Wiring Regulations practice mocks covering BS 7671 scope, definitions, protection, selection and erection, inspection and testing, special locations and appendices.
format: Twenty-two rotating 56-60-question practice mocks. Exam format: 120 minutes, open book. Pass at 60%+.

scoring.label: Pass — review the missed clauses and tables
Near miss — practise navigation through BS 7671
Major gaps — rebuild 18th Edition structure and lookup skills

priorities: BS 7671 scope, exclusions, definitions and the seven-part structure.
Protection for safety: ADS, RCDs, SPDs, overcurrent, thermal effects and isolation.
Selection and erection: wiring systems, current-carrying capacity, voltage drop and appendices.
Inspection, testing, certification and special installations or locations.
Use regulation-book logic; these mocks test close wording and table lookup judgement.

contentSources.limitations: Imported study-bank wording is an exam convention, not a substitute for the current official law, standard or guidance. Question-specific verified references take precedence where present.

questions.prompt: BS7671 applies to the design, erection and verification of which of the following?

options.B: Equipment on board ships covered by BS 8450

questions.explanation: BS 7671 covers the design, erection and verification of many fixed electrical installations, including caravan parks and similar sites. Ships, mines/quarries and railway traction equipment are separate exclusions or specialist systems.

A.text: BS 7671 covers the design, erection and verification of many fixed electrical installations, including caravan parks and similar sites. Ships, mines/quarries and railway traction equipment are separate exclusions or specialist systems.

B.text: Shipboard equipment covered by its own marine standard is outside the normal scope of BS 7671.

C.text: Mine and quarry aspects governed by specific statutory requirements are excluded from this installation standard.

D.text: Railway traction, rolling stock and signalling use specialist rules rather than the general BS 7671 scope.

questions.prompt: With regard to additions and alterations to installations, which of the following needs to be considered?

options.C: Rating and condition of existing equipment

questions.explanation: Before altering an installation, the existing equipment must be suitable for the changed load and safety requirements. Its rating and condition determine whether the alteration can be made without making the installation unsafe.

A.text: An installation method is selected for the new work; it does not establish whether existing equipment can safely accept the addition.

B.text: Cable-run length affects the new circuit calculations but does not prove the rating and condition of equipment already installed.

C.text: Before altering an installation, the existing equipment must be suitable for the changed load and safety requirements. Its rating and condition determine whether the alteration can be made without making the installation unsafe.

D.text: Programme and site access are project-management matters, not the electrical compatibility check required before an alteration.

questions.prompt: Ideally a characteristic of supply that should be allowed for before an installation design can begin is

options.A: Amount of socket outlets to be installed
options.B: Nature of current AC or DC
options.C: Proximity of persons to supply intake
options.D: The nature of installation of the distribution cabling

questions.explanation: The designer needs to know the nature of the supply before choosing equipment and protective measures. AC or DC supply affects device selection, fault behavior and cable calculations.

A.text: The number of socket-outlets is developed from the load and use requirements after the supply characteristics are known.

B.text: The designer needs to know the nature of the supply before choosing equipment and protective measures. AC or DC supply affects device selection, fault behavior and cable calculations.

C.text: Proximity of people is an external-influence and utilisation issue, not a characteristic of the incoming supply.

D.text: Distribution-cable installation is a design choice; it cannot tell the designer whether the source supplies AC or DC.

questions.prompt: It is recommended that every installation is subject to Periodic Inspection in accordance with Chapter
questions.explanation: Chapter 65 covers periodic inspection and testing of existing installations. It is the part used to decide how an installation is periodically assessed and reported on after it is in service.

A.text: Chapter 25 falls within definitions and general principles rather than the periodic-verification requirements.

B.text: Chapter 35 does not contain the requirements governing periodic inspection of an existing installation.

C.text: Chapter 55 covers other equipment matters, whereas periodic verification is set out in Chapter 65.

D.text: Chapter 65 covers periodic inspection and testing of existing installations. It is the part used to decide how an installation is periodically assessed and reported on after it is in service.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would describe someone with enough technical knowledge or practical experience appropriate to the work undertaken and to be capable of avoiding electrical danger, risk or hazards?
questions.explanation: A skilled person (electrically) has the technical knowledge or practical experience needed to recognize and avoid electrical danger. The wording is more specific than a general competent or instructed person.

A.text: Competence is a broad capability concept; the BS 7671 definition requested here is specifically a skilled person electrically.

B.text: A skilled person (electrically) has the technical knowledge or practical experience needed to recognize and avoid electrical danger. The wording is more specific than a general competent or instructed person.

C.text: Technical person is not the defined BS 7671 category for someone able to avoid electrical dangers independently.

D.text: An instructed person has been adequately advised or supervised but does not necessarily possess the skilled person's own expertise.

questions.prompt: A current passing through the body of a person or livestock such as to cause electric shock and likely to cause dangerous effects would be?
questions.explanation: Shock current is current passing through a person or livestock and capable of causing electric shock or dangerous physiological effects. Earth fault, leakage and short-circuit currents describe different fault or circuit conditions.

A.text: Earth-fault current flows because of an insulation fault to Earth; it is not defined by current passing through a body.

B.text: Earth-leakage current can flow in normal operation through insulation or capacitance without producing the described bodily shock.

C.text: Shock current is current passing through a person or livestock and capable of causing electric shock or dangerous physiological effects. Earth fault, leakage and short-circuit currents describe different fault or circuit conditions.

D.text: Short-circuit current follows an unintended low-impedance path between live conductors, not necessarily through a person or animal.

questions.prompt: Which earthing arrangement has one point of the source directly earthed while the installation's exposed-conductive-parts are connected to earth electrodes electrically independent of the source electrode?
questions.explanation: That is a TT system. One point of the source is directly earthed, while exposed-conductive-parts of the installation are connected to one or more local earth electrodes that are electrically independent of the source electrode.

A.text: An IT source is isolated from Earth or connected through a high impedance, unlike the directly earthed source described.

B.text: PME is a TN-C-S arrangement in which the supply PEN is multiply earthed; the installation does not use an independent TT electrode arrangement.

C.text: TN-S keeps neutral and protective conductors separate but connects exposed-conductive-parts back to the source earth.

D.text: That is a TT system. One point of the source is directly earthed, while exposed-conductive-parts of the installation are connected to one or more local earth electrodes that are electrically independent of the source electrode.

questions.prompt: Which of the following characteristics will be considered in relation to continuity of service?

options.B: Selection of the protective device in order to achieve selectivity
options.C: Size and future proofing of containment system

questions.explanation: Continuity of service is improved when protective devices are selected for selectivity, so only the faulty circuit disconnects. This avoids unnecessarily losing healthy parts of the installation.

A.text: Maximum demand sizes the supply and equipment; by itself it does not coordinate devices so one fault leaves other circuits available.

B.text: Continuity of service is improved when protective devices are selected for selectivity, so only the faulty circuit disconnects. This avoids unnecessarily losing healthy parts of the installation.

C.text: Future containment capacity helps later expansion but does not provide protective-device selectivity during a present fault.

D.text: A wiring-system type must suit its environment, yet continuity depends on how protective devices and supplies are coordinated.

questions.prompt: Every installation shall be divided into circuits as necessary, in order to

options.A: Meet the needs of clients with disabilities
options.B: Eliminate the need for earth-fault protection
options.C: Prevent the de-energization of a circuit intended to be isolated
options.D: Reduce the possibility of unwanted RCD tripping due to excessive protective conductor currents not due to a fault

questions.explanation: Dividing circuits helps avoid unwanted RCD tripping caused by accumulated protective-conductor currents that are not due to a fault. Circuit division cannot eliminate the need for earth-fault protection; it limits the consequences of faults and supports safe operation and maintenance.

A.text: Accessibility needs influence equipment and controls, but this option is not the circuit-division objective being tested.

B.text: Circuit division cannot remove the requirement for earth-fault protection; every affected circuit still needs an effective protective measure.

C.text: De-energising a circuit intended to be isolated is the purpose of isolation, not an outcome that circuit division should prevent.

D.text: Dividing circuits helps avoid unwanted RCD tripping caused by accumulated protective-conductor currents that are not due to a fault. Circuit division cannot eliminate the need for earth-fault protection; it limits the consequences of faults and supports safe operation and maintenance.

questions.prompt: With regard to electromagnetic compatibility, what shall meet the appropriate EMC compatibility requirements?
questions.explanation: EMC requirements apply to electrical equipment generally, because any item can emit disturbance or be affected by disturbance. The aim is for equipment to operate together without harmful interference.

A.text: EMC requirements apply to electrical equipment generally, because any item can emit disturbance or be affected by disturbance. The aim is for equipment to operate together without harmful interference.

B.text: Data cabling is only one part of an installation and cannot stand in for the EMC obligations on every item of electrical equipment.

C.text: Life-support equipment needs particularly careful EMC control, but the requirement is not limited to that specialist category.

D.text: Sockets and switches are a small equipment subset; limiting compliance to them would leave active equipment and wiring interfaces unchecked.

questions.prompt: Which of the following comprises of having a protective conductor that is the metallic covering of the cable supplying the installation or a separate conductor?
questions.explanation: TN-S uses a separate protective conductor from the source, often the metallic sheath or covering of the supply cable or a separate conductor. Neutral and protective functions remain separate in the installation.

A.text: An IT system has no direct source-earth connection or uses a high impedance, so this cable-sheath return description does not define it.

B.text: PME uses a combined PEN in the supply and separate protective and neutral conductors in the installation, rather than the stated TN-S arrangement.

C.text: TN-S uses a separate protective conductor from the source, often the metallic sheath or covering of the supply cable or a separate conductor. Neutral and protective functions remain separate in the installation.

D.text: A TT installation connects exposed-conductive-parts to a local electrode independent of the source electrode, not through the supply cable covering.

questions.prompt: Which listed supply is not, by itself, an independent electrical source for a safety service?

options.A: A generator set independent of the normal supply
options.C: Primary cells selected for the required duty
options.D: Storage batteries selected for the required duty

questions.explanation: The normal DNO supply alone is the supply whose failure the safety service must withstand, so it is not an independent safety source. Suitable independent generating sets and correctly selected battery sources are recognised ways of supplying safety services.

A.text: An independent generating set can maintain a safety service when the normal supply fails, so it is a valid safety source.

B.text: The normal DNO supply alone is the supply whose failure the safety service must withstand, so it is not an independent safety source. Suitable independent generating sets and correctly selected battery sources are recognised ways of supplying safety services.

C.text: Correctly selected primary cells store energy independently of the DNO supply and can serve the required safety load.

D.text: Storage batteries provide an independent reserve source and are commonly used for safety services such as emergency lighting.

questions.prompt: Chapter 41 specifies essential requirements regarding protection against electric shock. What else does it deal with?

options.B: Selection and erection of wiring systems
options.C: The application and coordination of installation protection with regard to external influences

questions.explanation: Chapter 41 covers the application and coordination of protective measures for electric shock in relation to external influences. Conductor colour identification is dealt with in Section 514, not Chapter 41; replacing the original disconnection-time option removes a second defensible answer.

A.text: Requirements for parallel conductors belong with wiring-system selection and current-sharing design, not the additional Chapter 41 subject asked here.

B.text: Selection and erection of wiring systems is principally a Chapter 52 matter rather than the coordination of shock-protection measures.

C.text: Chapter 41 covers the application and coordination of protective measures for electric shock in relation to external influences. Conductor colour identification is dealt with in Section 514, not Chapter 41; replacing the original disconnection-time option removes a second defensible answer.

D.text: Conductor colour identification is addressed in Section 514 and does not describe Chapter 41's treatment of external influences.

questions.prompt: To provide additional protection for automatic disconnection of supplies, RCDs may be used provided their residual current values are rated at no more than
questions.explanation: A 30 mA RCD is the usual upper limit for additional protection against electric shock. Higher residual-current ratings may provide other protection, but they do not give the same additional personal protection.

A.text: A 100 mA RCD is too insensitive to qualify as the 30 mA additional protection specified for electric-shock risk.

B.text: A 30 mA RCD is the usual upper limit for additional protection against electric shock. Higher residual-current ratings may provide other protection, but they do not give the same additional personal protection.

C.text: Thirty-two amperes is a load-current rating, not a rated residual operating current for additional protection.

D.text: A 50 mA residual rating exceeds the permitted 30 mA ceiling and therefore does not provide the specified additional protection.

questions.prompt: In each installation main protective bonding conductors shall be provided to which of the following?

options.C: Metal pipes that enter a building that have an insulated section at the point of entry

questions.explanation: Main protective bonding connects extraneous-conductive-parts such as exposed metallic structural parts to the main earthing terminal. This keeps accessible metalwork at substantially the same potential during faults.

A.text: Main protective bonding connects extraneous-conductive-parts such as exposed metallic structural parts to the main earthing terminal. This keeps accessible metalwork at substantially the same potential during faults.

B.text: Local bathroom pipework that cannot introduce an external potential is not automatically a main-bonding connection at the origin.

C.text: An insulating section at entry prevents the external metal pipe from introducing Earth potential, so main bonding is not established by this description.

D.text: A radiator is normally part of the building's internal services and is not automatically an extraneous-conductive-part requiring main bonding.

questions.prompt: Which listed power-electronic device is a common source of electromagnetic disturbance because it converts DC to AC by rapid switching?
questions.explanation: An inverter uses rapidly switched power semiconductors to synthesize an AC output. Its switching edges can produce conducted and radiated electromagnetic disturbance, so the installation design must consider filtering, bonding, screening, routing and separation.

A.text: A passive capacitor can affect power factor or filtering, but it does not synthesize AC through rapid semiconductor switching.

B.text: An incandescent lamp is mainly a resistive load and does not create the high-frequency switching edges characteristic of an inverter.

C.text: An inverter uses rapidly switched power semiconductors to synthesize an AC output. Its switching edges can produce conducted and radiated electromagnetic disturbance, so the installation design must consider filtering, bonding, screening, routing and separation.

D.text: A correctly arranged busbar distributes power without performing the DC-to-AC switching conversion described in the question.

questions.prompt: For the five-second disconnection condition, what maximum earth fault loop impedance is listed for a 30 A BS 3036 fuse?
questions.explanation: The Chapter 41 table value for a 30 A BS 3036 fuse under the five-second condition is 2.51 Ω. The circuit's maximum Zs must not exceed that value at the conductor operating temperature.

A.text: 1.04 ohms is more restrictive than the listed five-second limit and therefore is not the maximum value requested.

B.text: 1.51 ohms remains below the applicable 2.51-ohm boundary, so it cannot be the table's maximum permitted value.

C.text: The Chapter 41 table value for a 30 A BS 3036 fuse under the five-second condition is 2.51 Ω. The circuit's maximum Zs must not exceed that value at the conductor operating temperature.

D.text: 1.67 ohms is also below the stated five-second limit and would unnecessarily reject compliant loop-impedance results.

questions.prompt: The protective measures of obstacles and placing out of reach are restricted to installations accessible only to whom?

options.D: Skilled persons, or instructed persons under the supervision of skilled persons

questions.explanation: Obstacles and placing out of reach provide only basic protection and can be deliberately bypassed. They are therefore restricted to controlled installations accessible only to skilled persons or instructed persons acting under skilled supervision.

A.text: A sports venue may admit the general public, so its use does not establish the controlled access these measures require.

B.text: Ordinary people without electrical instruction may deliberately bypass an obstacle and cannot rely on this restricted basic-protection measure.

C.text: An instructed person alone is insufficient unless acting under the supervision of a skilled person in the controlled installation.

D.text: Obstacles and placing out of reach provide only basic protection and can be deliberately bypassed. They are therefore restricted to controlled installations accessible only to skilled persons or instructed persons acting under skilled supervision.

questions.prompt: What minimum IP degree, stated using the first characteristic numeral, applies to readily accessible horizontal top surfaces of barriers or enclosures?
questions.explanation: Readily accessible horizontal top surfaces must provide at least IP4X protection. IP2X is the normal minimum for other barrier or enclosure surfaces; the corrected stem asks specifically for the digit-form designation and removes the malformed alternative.

A.text: IP2X is the normal enclosure minimum elsewhere, but a readily accessible horizontal top needs the finer IP4X protection.

B.text: Readily accessible horizontal top surfaces must provide at least IP4X protection. IP2X is the normal minimum for other barrier or enclosure surfaces; the corrected stem asks specifically for the digit-form designation and removes the malformed alternative.

C.text: IP65 adds dust-tight and water-jet protection that the question does not require, so it is not the minimum degree asked for.

D.text: IP3X still permits access by a larger probe than IP4X and is insufficient for the accessible horizontal top surface.

questions.prompt: For a socket-outlet covered by the current Regulation 411.3.3 risk-assessment exception, what must justify omission of 30 mA RCD protection?

options.B: An as fitted drawing detailing those sockets not protected
options.C: A suitably documented risk assessment undertaken with the involvement of a skilled person (electrically)
options.D: Retention of a disclaimer from the client or designer

questions.explanation: The limited exception requires a suitably documented risk assessment undertaken with the involvement of a skilled person (electrically). It does not apply to socket-outlets used by ordinary persons, children or disabled persons, or to outdoor mobile equipment covered by the other indents.

A.text: A maximum-demand assessment establishes loading, not whether omitting life-safety RCD additional protection is acceptable.

B.text: An as-fitted drawing records the arrangement but does not evaluate the likelihood and consequences of electric shock.

C.text: The limited exception requires a suitably documented risk assessment undertaken with the involvement of a skilled person (electrically). It does not apply to socket-outlets used by ordinary persons, children or disabled persons, or to outdoor mobile equipment covered by the other indents.

D.text: A disclaimer cannot transfer away the designer's safety duties or replace a documented electrical risk assessment.

questions.prompt: Under the current Regulation 443.4.1 default for cases not involving serious injury, loss of life, or significant financial or data loss, when may transient-overvoltage protection be omitted?

options.A: Only when the owner declares the possible loss or damage tolerable, accepts the risk and the decision is recorded
options.B: Whenever the calculated prospective short-circuit current is below 16 kA
options.C: Whenever the installation is a single dwelling
options.D: Whenever local lightning records show no strike in the previous year

questions.explanation: The obsolete calculated risk level method is no longer the BS 7671 decision rule. In other cases the default is to provide protection unless the owner declares that possible loss or damage is tolerable, accepts the risk and the decision is recorded on the certification.

A.text: The obsolete calculated risk level method is no longer the BS 7671 decision rule. In other cases the default is to provide protection unless the owner declares that possible loss or damage is tolerable, accepts the risk and the decision is recorded on the certification.

B.text: Prospective short-circuit current concerns fault-breaking capacity and is not the decision threshold for omitting surge protection.

C.text: A dwelling is not automatically exempt; the owner must make and record the specified tolerability decision where omission is allowed.

D.text: One quiet year of local lightning history does not establish tolerable equipment, data or financial consequences over the installation's life.

questions.prompt: When it comes to isolation and switching, in general the PEN conductor shall not be isolated or switched in
questions.explanation: A PEN conductor combines neutral and protective functions, so opening it can remove the earth reference and leave exposed metalwork dangerous. That is why PEN conductors are generally not isolated or switched in TN-C and TN-C-S systems.

A.text: IT and TT systems do not contain a supply PEN conductor, so they are not the pair governed by this prohibition.

B.text: An IT system keeps its source isolated or impedance-earthed and therefore has no PEN conductor to leave unswitched.

C.text: A PEN conductor combines neutral and protective functions, so opening it can remove the earth reference and leave exposed metalwork dangerous. That is why PEN conductors are generally not isolated or switched in TN-C and TN-C-S systems.

D.text: TT has separate neutral and protective arrangements; pairing it with TN-C misses the TN-C-S system that also uses a supply PEN.

questions.prompt: Where emergency switching is required because of a risk of electric shock, which conductors must the device disconnect?
questions.explanation: Emergency switching for an electric-shock risk must disconnect all live conductors with one action. Protective and functional earthing conductors are not substituted for live-conductor isolation, and neutral-only switching would leave line conductors energised.

A.text: Neutral-only switching can leave line conductors energised, so it cannot remove the electric-shock hazard in one action.

B.text: Emergency switching for an electric-shock risk must disconnect all live conductors with one action. Protective and functional earthing conductors are not substituted for live-conductor isolation, and neutral-only switching would leave line conductors energised.

C.text: Opening a circuit protective conductor would remove the safety path while live conductors could remain energised.

D.text: A functional earthing conductor serves operational purposes and is not a substitute for disconnecting every live conductor.

questions.prompt: In busbar installations, where the equipment is rated at 200A per phase or more, the earthing busbar must have a CSA of at least,
questions.explanation: A large busbar installation needs a substantial earthing busbar so it can carry fault current safely. For equipment rated 200 A per phase or more, the minimum cross-sectional area in the question is 50 mm2.

A.text: 100 square millimetres is above the stipulated minimum, so it may be adequate but is not the minimum size requested.

B.text: 25 square millimetres is below the minimum for the stated 200 A-per-phase busbar arrangement.

C.text: 35 square millimetres also falls short of the 50-square-millimetre minimum protective busbar cross-section.

D.text: A large busbar installation needs a substantial earthing busbar so it can carry fault current safely. For equipment rated 200 A per phase or more, the minimum cross-sectional area in the question is 50 mm2.

questions.prompt: Where a cable screen has insufficient conductivity for the expected common-mode current, which additional conductor can reduce electromagnetic interference?

options.A: A bypass conductor connected in parallel with the screen
options.B: A bridge rectifier in the load circuit
options.C: Oversized line and neutral conductors with no bonding change
options.D: Unbonded containment around only part of the route

questions.explanation: A low-impedance bypass conductor bonded in parallel with the screen can carry common-mode current and reinforce the screen path. Rectifiers, oversized live conductors or incomplete unbonded containment do not provide that controlled EMC return path.

A.text: A low-impedance bypass conductor bonded in parallel with the screen can carry common-mode current and reinforce the screen path. Rectifiers, oversized live conductors or incomplete unbonded containment do not provide that controlled EMC return path.

B.text: A bridge rectifier changes waveform and can itself create harmonics; it does not reinforce the cable screen's return path.

C.text: Larger live conductors do not provide a low-impedance parallel path for common-mode current around an inadequate screen.

D.text: Partly surrounding the route with unbonded containment creates no continuous controlled screen and can worsen coupling.

questions.prompt: Under current Regulation 421.1.7, in which premises are AFDDs required for the specified single-phase AC final circuits supplying socket-outlets or fixed current-using equipment rated not more than 32 A?

options.A: Every circuit on board a ship
options.C: Higher-risk residential buildings, houses in multiple occupation, purpose-built student accommodation and care homes
options.D: Electric-fence circuits covered by their product standard

questions.explanation: Regulation 421.1.7 requires AFDDs for the specified single-phase final circuits in higher-risk residential buildings, HMOs, purpose-built student accommodation and care homes. AFDDs are recommended more widely, but the old wording describing only a recommendation in combustible locations is obsolete.

A.text: Ship circuits are outside the normal installation scope and AFDDs are not universally mandated for every circuit on a vessel.

B.text: Radio-interference suppression is an EMC function, not one of the premises categories where Regulation 421.1.7 mandates AFDDs.

C.text: Regulation 421.1.7 requires AFDDs for the specified single-phase final circuits in higher-risk residential buildings, HMOs, purpose-built student accommodation and care homes. AFDDs are recommended more widely, but the old wording describing only a recommendation in combustible locations is obsolete.

D.text: Electric-fence circuits follow their specialist product and installation rules and are not the defined residential AFDD category.

questions.prompt: What maximum disconnection time applies to a 230 V AC TT final circuit covered by the Table 41.1 final-circuit condition?
questions.explanation: For a 230 V AC TT final circuit within the Table 41.1 condition, the maximum disconnection time is 0.2 s. The stray '0.4 seconds' text in the original stem contradicted the keyed TT value.

solutionTables.title: Focused standards lookup

source.edition: Edition not recorded in the source question
source.licence: Reference only — full BSI/IET table not reproduced

solutionTables.note: This is a focused study lookup generated from the question's cited source and keyed answer, not a reproduction of the full standards table. Verify it against the exact edition required by your course or assessment.

A.text: 0.07 seconds is shorter than the Table 41.1 maximum for the stated 230 V TT final circuit.

B.text: For a 230 V AC TT final circuit within the Table 41.1 condition, the maximum disconnection time is 0.2 s. The stray '0.4 seconds' text in the original stem contradicted the keyed TT value.

C.text: 0.4 seconds is the corresponding TN final-circuit value at 230 V, not the TT limit asked for.

D.text: Thirty milliseconds is not the Table 41.1 TT disconnection boundary and confuses a time value with very rapid device operation.

questions.prompt: With regard to electrical connections, every connection shall be accessible for inspection and testing purposes except in the case of the following example

options.A: A compound filled or encapsulated joint
options.B: A connection made in roof spaces or ceilings
options.D: A joint designed to be installed in lightning protection systems

questions.explanation: Most connections must be accessible so they can be inspected, tested and maintained. A compound-filled or encapsulated joint is an exception because it is sealed and intended not to be opened for normal inspection.

A.text: Most connections must be accessible so they can be inspected, tested and maintained. A compound-filled or encapsulated joint is an exception because it is sealed and intended not to be opened for normal inspection.

B.text: A connection in a roof void still needs access unless it uses a recognised maintenance-free or encapsulated construction.

C.text: Floor concealment alone does not create an exception; a conventional connection remains accessible for inspection and testing.

D.text: A lightning-protection joint is not automatically exempt merely because of its intended system; the construction and location determine access.

questions.prompt: Where a PEN conductor is installed it should be identified by the use of the following coloured marks

options.A: Green-and-yellow throughout its length with additional blue marking at the terminations
options.C: Green and yellow throughout it's length

questions.explanation: A PEN conductor combines protective and neutral functions. It is identified green-and-yellow throughout its length with additional blue marking at its terminations, so both functions are unambiguous.

A.text: A PEN conductor combines protective and neutral functions. It is identified green-and-yellow throughout its length with additional blue marking at its terminations, so both functions are unambiguous.

B.text: Cream is not a recognised protective or neutral conductor colour in the BS 7671 identification scheme.

C.text: Green-and-yellow alone shows a protective function but omits the blue termination marking needed for the PEN neutral function.

D.text: Single green is prohibited for conductor identification and also fails to show either required PEN colour arrangement.

questions.prompt: Which listed metallic cable component may serve as a protective conductor without separate colour identification along its length?

options.A: An individual insulated conductor with no identification
options.B: The steel-wire armour of a cable used as a protective conductor
options.C: An unidentified core used as a switched line conductor
options.D: An unidentified live conductor in a two-wire DC circuit

questions.explanation: A cable's metallic sheath or armour used as a protective conductor need not be colour-marked along its inaccessible length, though its function must be clear at terminations. Individual insulated conductors still require the prescribed identification.

A.text: An individual insulated conductor cannot be left unidentified because its function must remain clear throughout installation and maintenance.

B.text: A cable's metallic sheath or armour used as a protective conductor need not be colour-marked along its inaccessible length, though its function must be clear at terminations. Individual insulated conductors still require the prescribed identification.

C.text: A switched-line core needs the prescribed line identification at its accessible terminations; being used for switching creates no blanket exemption.

D.text: Live conductors in a two-wire DC circuit require the applicable polarity identification rather than being left unmarked.

questions.prompt: What is the derating factor for a cable installed within 200 mm of thermal insulation?
questions.explanation: Thermal insulation prevents heat escaping from a cable, so the cable cannot carry as much current. The 0.63 factor reduces the current-carrying capacity for the stated 200 mm insulation condition.

A.text: A factor of 0.51 applies to a more severe thermal-insulation condition than the stated 200 mm contact length.

B.text: Thermal insulation prevents heat escaping from a cable, so the cable cannot carry as much current. The 0.63 factor reduces the current-carrying capacity for the stated 200 mm insulation condition.

C.text: A factor of 0.78 would allow more current than the 200 mm insulation arrangement permits and risks overheating.

D.text: A factor of 0.88 gives too little derating for this degree of contact with thermal insulation.

questions.prompt: Which listed conductor characteristic must be taken into account when selecting a terminal or connection method under Regulation 526.2?

options.C: The cross sectional area of the conductor

questions.explanation: The terminal or connection method must be suitable for the conductor's cross-sectional area. Regulation 526.2 also considers conductor material, insulation, number and shape of wires and the number of conductors being connected.

A.text: Accessibility determines whether a connection can be inspected, but it is not a physical characteristic of the conductor entering the terminal.

B.text: Ambient temperature affects equipment selection generally; the specific terminal check here is compatibility with conductor cross-sectional area.

C.text: The terminal or connection method must be suitable for the conductor's cross-sectional area. Regulation 526.2 also considers conductor material, insulation, number and shape of wires and the number of conductors being connected.

D.text: Circuit voltage sets insulation and equipment ratings, not whether the terminal can securely accommodate the conductor size.

questions.prompt: When a generator set is used as a safety source, it must comply with
questions.explanation: BS ISO 8528-12 covers reciprocating internal-combustion-engine-driven generating sets used for emergency power supply to safety services. The original option transposed the standard number and named a non-existent 'BS 7698-12'.

A.text: BS 1362 specifies domestic plug fuse-links and does not govern generating sets supplying safety services.

B.text: BS 3036 covers semi-enclosed fuses, not the design and performance of an emergency generating set.

C.text: BS ISO 8528-12 covers reciprocating internal-combustion-engine-driven generating sets used for emergency power supply to safety services. The original option transposed the standard number and named a non-existent 'BS 7698-12'.

D.text: Building control recommendations cannot replace the dedicated generating-set product standard required for this safety source.

questions.prompt: Two or more circuits are allowed in the same conduit, ducting or trunking system provided the requirements of?

options.B: The appropriate calculations have been carried out

questions.prompt: Choose one of the following which does not fall under compatibility?

questions.prompt: Where a generating set is used as an additional source of supply in parallel with other sources, it shall be installed

options.A: On the load side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with no additional requirements
options.B: On the load side of all the protective devices to the final circuit which must be connected by plug and socket

options.D: On the supply side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with no additional requirements

questions.explanation: A generating set operating in parallel is connected on the supply side of the final-circuit protective devices. A.text: On the load side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with no additional requirements would bypass or mis-coordinate upstream protection and isolation when the generator operates in parallel.

questions.prompt: Regarding auxiliary supplies to safety services, the maximum changeover time refers to

options.A: How long the safety source can supply the rated power output to the safety service

questions.explanation: Maximum changeover time is how long it takes the safety source to supply the safety service after the normal supply fails. It is about transfer delay, not how long the standby source can run.

A.text: How long the safety source can supply the rated power output to the safety service is the source's rated duration or autonomy, measured after it has taken over the load.

B.text: How often maintenance has to be carried out on the auxiliary supply is a service interval and says nothing about how quickly the safety supply becomes available after failure.

C.text: The frequency (in cycles per second) of the auxiliary supply feeding the safety service is electrical frequency, not elapsed transfer time following loss of the normal source.

D.text: Maximum changeover time is how long it takes the safety source to supply the safety service after the normal supply fails. It is about transfer delay, not how long the standby source can run.

questions.prompt: The protective conductor used within a final circuit has high protective conductor currents in excess of 10 mA when supplying more than one item of electrical equipment. The minimal cross-sectional area may be 4 mm², provided that:

questions.prompt: The IEE Regulations recognises that in electrical installations there is a risk of injury from:
questions.explanation: The Regulations are concerned chiefly with the hazards arising directly from electricity itself. Among these, the risk of injury from shock currents passing through the body is a central danger the requirements are designed to prevent.

B.text: Hazardous chemicals need COSHH controls; their toxicity is not an injury mechanism created by current flowing in an electrical installation.

C.text: High wind is an external influence on equipment selection, not the direct electrical injury mechanism that shock protection is designed to limit.

D.text: The Regulations are concerned chiefly with the hazards arising directly from electricity itself. Among these, the risk of injury from shock currents passing through the body is a central danger the requirements are designed to prevent.

questions.prompt: When choosing the type of wiring system for an installation, consideration should be given to:

options.A: Accessibility of wiring to persons and livestock
options.B: The experience of the installing electrician

questions.explanation: Selecting a wiring system involves considering the external influences it will face in service. Whether wiring is accessible to people and livestock affects the risk of damage and contact, so this must be weighed when choosing a suitable method.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 requires that:

options.A: All installations have a main switch
options.B: The installation main switch switches the line conductor only
options.C: The main switch must have BS 88 fuses
options.D: There must be an effective means of cutting off all voltages of every installation

A.text: Some installations legitimately use more than one device or arrangement for isolation, so one physical main switch is not a universal form requirement.

B.text: Opening only line is insufficient where another live conductor can retain a hazardous voltage; isolation must address every relevant live source.

C.text: A main switch performs switching and isolation; fitting BS 88 fuses is neither necessary for that function nor required in every installation.

D.text: Every installation must be capable of being made safe for work or in an emergency. The Regulations therefore require an effective means of cutting off all voltages, so the supply can be fully isolated rather than partially disconnected.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 requires that the person carrying out the inspection and testing shall:

options.A: Be competent to carry out the testing
options.D: Have at least three years' experience

questions.explanation: Reliable inspection and testing depends on the judgement and knowledge of the individual carrying it out. The Regulations require that person to be competent for the work, since only sound competence ensures faults are correctly identified and the installation verified as safe.

A.text: Reliable inspection and testing depends on the judgement and knowledge of the individual carrying it out. The Regulations require that person to be competent for the work, since only sound competence ensures faults are correctly identified and the installation verified as safe.

B.text: A periodic report is produced only for periodic verification; initial verification instead uses the certificate and schedules appropriate to the new work.

questions.prompt: An overcurrent occurring in a circuit that is electrically sound is defined as:
questions.explanation: An overload is an overcurrent that arises in a circuit with no electrical fault, where the conductors and insulation remain intact but the load drawn simply exceeds the circuit's rated capacity. D.text: A short circuit is a low-impedance fault between live conductors, whereas an overload leaves the circuit electrically intact and simply draws too much current.

questions.prompt: The term fault protection refers to:

options.D: Protection against electric shock under fault conditions

B.text: Insulated enclosures prevent normal contact with live parts and therefore provide basic protection rather than protection after insulation failure.

C.text: Dust ingress is controlled by enclosure selection and IP rating; it is separate from limiting shock when exposed metal becomes live under fault conditions.

D.text: Fault protection guards against electric shock when a fault, such as a breakdown of basic insulation, makes an exposed-conductive-part live. Measures like automatic disconnection of supply ensure dangerous touch voltages are removed quickly under those fault conditions, protecting anyone in contact.

questions.prompt: The design current of a circuit is the current:

options.A: A fuse is designed to carry

questions.explanation: Design current is the current intended to be carried by a circuit during normal service. It forms the starting point for sizing conductors and selecting the protective device, since the cable and device must comfortably handle the expected working load.

D.text: The protective-device rating In is selected around the design current but is not itself the current the connected equipment is expected to draw.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is an exposed conductive part?

options.C: The casing of a central heating pump
options.D: The casing of Class II equipment

questions.explanation: An exposed-conductive-part is conductive metalwork of equipment that can be touched and is not normally live but could become live under a fault. The pump casing fits this, whereas pipes and radiators are extraneous parts and Class II equipment has no such reliance on earthing.

A.text: A radiator is normally extraneous metalwork connected to a service, not electrical equipment with a casing that could become live from its own insulation fault.

B.text: A water pipe can introduce Earth potential and may need bonding, but it is not an exposed-conductive-part of current-using equipment.

C.text: An exposed-conductive-part is conductive metalwork of equipment that can be touched and is not normally live but could become live under a fault. The pump casing fits this, whereas pipes and radiators are extraneous parts and Class II equipment has no such reliance on earthing.

questions.prompt: A short circuit current is defined as:

options.B: An over current occurring in an electrically sound circuit
options.C: The current occurring during a fault between live conductors of negligible impedance
options.D: The current rating of the fuse

questions.explanation: A short-circuit current is the overcurrent resulting from a fault of negligible impedance between conductors normally at different potentials, such as line and neutral. Because the connecting path has almost no resistance, the prospective current can be very large and demands rapid disconnection.

questions.prompt: A d.c. voltage of 80V between conductors is classified as being:
questions.explanation: Voltage bands place anything not exceeding 120V d.c. between conductors within extra-low voltage. At 80V d.c. the circuit sits comfortably below that threshold, so it is classified as extra-low rather than low voltage.

questions.prompt: The part of a fuse that is designed to melt when the fuse operates is called the fuse____
questions.explanation: The element is the calibrated conductive part within a fuse that carries normal current but heats and melts when an overcurrent persists. Its controlled melting breaks the circuit, while the carrier and link simply hold or connect the fuse in place.

C.text: A fuse link is the complete replaceable unit containing the calibrated element, not only the part intended to melt.

D.text: Ordinary wire is not a controlled protective element unless manufactured and calibrated as part of the correct fuse system.

questions.prompt: A person with technical knowledge or sufficient experience to enable him/her to avoid dangers that electricity may create is defined as:
questions.explanation: A skilled person is defined by their technical knowledge or experience, enabling them to recognise and avoid the dangers electricity can create. This goes beyond an instructed person, who only works safely under the supervision or guidance of a skilled person.

B.text: Training contributes to competence, but 'trained person' is not the defined BS 7671 category described by this knowledge-and-experience wording.

C.text: An instructed person relies on adequate instruction or supervision and does not necessarily have the independent expertise described in the stem.

D.text: An ordinary person is neither skilled nor instructed in electrical matters and cannot be assumed to recognise and avoid electrical dangers.

questions.prompt: Protective conductor current is a current that:

options.B: Appears in a protective conductor such as leakage current

questions.explanation: Protective conductor current is the current that flows in a protective conductor under normal, healthy conditions, for example the leakage current arising from equipment with filters or capacitive coupling. It exists without any fault present, unlike an earth fault current.

A.text: Normal leakage can remain well below an RCD threshold, so protective-conductor current does not automatically trip a residual-current device.

B.text: Protective conductor current is the current that flows in a protective conductor under normal, healthy conditions, for example the leakage current arising from equipment with filters or capacitive coupling. It exists without any fault present, unlike an earth fault current.

questions.prompt: An overload current could arise when:

options.A: A forward/reverse controller attempts to switch a motor to both directions simultaneously
options.B: An electrician drills through a busbar chamber and touches a live busbar with the drill
options.C: Contamination of a motor terminal block results in tracking
options.D: Excessive mechanical load is applied to an electric motor

questions.explanation: An overload occurs in a sound circuit when the connected load demands more current than intended, such as a motor asked to drive an excessive mechanical load. The conductors remain undamaged, so the rise in current is overload rather than a fault current.

B.text: A drill contacting a live busbar creates a short circuit or earth fault through damaged insulation and metalwork rather than a normal-service overload.

C.text: Tracking across a contaminated terminal block is an insulation fault path; the circuit is no longer electrically sound when that current flows.

D.text: An overload occurs in a sound circuit when the connected load demands more current than intended, such as a motor asked to drive an excessive mechanical load. The conductors remain undamaged, so the rise in current is overload rather than a fault current.

questions.prompt: The type of building construction in which an installation is to be carried out may affect the design and safe operation of the installation. This effect is called:
questions.explanation: Conditions arising from the surroundings, including the type of building construction, are treated as external influences that the designer must assess. These influences affect equipment selection and installation methods so that the installation operates safely in its particular environment.

These influences affect equipment selection and installation methods so that the installation operates safely in its particular environment.

C.text: Maintainability concerns access and expected maintenance quality; it is not the classification for combustible, moving or otherwise influential building fabric.

D.text: Nature of supply describes voltage, frequency and earthing arrangement delivered at the origin, not the structure through which wiring is installed.

questions.prompt: In addition to regular maintenance of an installation, which one of the following is NOT an essential requirement?

options.B: Protective measures for safety remain effective

questions.explanation: The essential maintenance requirements are that protective measures stay effective, equipment reliability is sustained, and periodic inspection and testing can be done safely. Displaying the contractor's name and address by the mains is not among these safety-related requirements.

C.text: The essential maintenance requirements are that protective measures stay effective, equipment reliability is sustained, and periodic inspection and testing can be done safely. Displaying the contractor's name and address by the mains is not among these safety-related requirements.

questions.prompt: The three general categories of external influence are environment, utilisation and:

questions.explanation: External influences are grouped into three broad categories: environment, utilisation, and the construction of buildings. questions.prompt: With reference to the general characteristics of an electrical installation, the maximum demand should be:

questions.prompt: The external influence having a classification of AD8 would indicate a condition of:

questions.prompt: Where a wiring system is installed in a building whose structure has an external influence category CB4, the wiring system shall be:

questions.prompt: An external influence categorised as AG1 applies to a:

questions.prompt: When considering continuity of service to life support systems, which one of the following should be considered?

questions.explanation: Continuity of supply to critical loads like life support depends on a fault clearing only the affected circuit, not the whole system. Selecting protective devices to achieve discrimination ensures the device nearest the fault operates first, leaving upstream supplies intact for essential equipment.

questions.prompt: A 230 V single-phase circuit supplying a pump motor is protected by a 20 A Type C circuit-breaker to BS EN 60898. What minimum fault current guarantees operation in the instantaneous range?
questions.explanation: Use the upper edge of the Type C instantaneous band, 10 × In, when operation must be guaranteed. For a 20 A device, Ia = 10 × 20 A = 200 A.

questions.prompt: Given that the fault current on a 16A BS 88 fuse is 60A, the corresponding disconnection time is:

questions.explanation: Following the BS 1361 cartridge fuse time/current characteristic for a 30 A device, a fault current of 200 A corresponds to a disconnection time of roughly 0.4 seconds. The cartridge construction clears faster than a rewireable fuse at the same overcurrent.
