questions.prompt: Which of the following does not fall under compatibility?
questions.explanation: Compatibility concerns whether equipment characteristics could harmfully affect other equipment or the supply, covering things like starting currents, power factor and transient overvoltages. Continuity of service is a separate consideration about maintaining supply, not a compatibility issue between connected equipment.

A.text: Compatibility concerns whether equipment characteristics could harmfully affect other equipment or the supply, covering things like starting currents, power factor and transient overvoltages. Continuity of service is a separate consideration about maintaining supply, not a compatibility issue between connected equipment.

B.text: Poor power factor increases current and can disturb or burden the supply, so it is a recognised compatibility characteristic.

C.text: Large starting currents can depress voltage and affect nearby equipment, making them a core equipment-compatibility issue.

D.text: Transient overvoltages can damage or upset other equipment, so insulation withstand and surge control form part of compatibility.

questions.prompt: The following are all reasons for dividing a circuit except

options.A: Allowing future expansion within the installation
options.B: Preventing dangers arising from nuisance tripping
options.C: Preventing the indirect energising of circuit intended to be isolated

questions.explanation: Division is required to limit fault consequences, reduce unwanted tripping, prevent indirect energization and reduce electromagnetic disturbance. Providing spare capacity for future expansion is sensible planning, but it is not one of those protective reasons.

A.text: Division is required to limit fault consequences, reduce unwanted tripping, prevent indirect energization and reduce electromagnetic disturbance. Providing spare capacity for future expansion is sensible planning, but it is not one of those protective reasons.

B.text: Dividing circuits limits the scope of unwanted tripping so a harmless leakage or local fault does not remove unrelated services and create danger.

C.text: Separate circuits help prevent backfeeds or shared connections from energizing a circuit that a worker reasonably believes has been isolated.

D.text: Separating noisy loads and sensitive wiring can reduce conducted and radiated interference between circuits sharing an installation.

questions.prompt: Which earthing system has the supply neutral earthed at the source and a separate protective conductor from source to installation?
questions.explanation: TN-S keeps neutral and protective conductors separate throughout the system, with the source neutral connected to Earth. C.text: TN-S keeps neutral and protective conductors separate throughout the system, with the source neutral connected to Earth. TN-C-S combines them as a PEN for part of the supply, TT uses the installation's own electrode, and IT has no direct source-earth connection or uses a high impedance.

questions.prompt: When protecting against burns a metallic part intended to be touched but not hand held shall be limited to a maximum temperature of:
questions.explanation: To prevent burns, an accessible metallic part intended to be touched but not gripped is limited to 70 degrees Celsius. Metal conducts heat readily, so this lower limit guards against skin injury during brief contact in normal service.

B.text: Seventy-five degrees exceeds the stated metallic touch-temperature limit and increases burn risk because metal transfers heat quickly to skin.

C.text: Eighty degrees is the allowance for a comparable non-metallic touched surface, not a metal surface with high thermal conductivity.

questions.explanation: For fixed equipment with a rating exceeding 32A on a 230V TN system, the maximum disconnection time is 5 seconds rather than 0.4 seconds. Larger fixed circuits are permitted the longer time because the touch-voltage risk is managed differently than for socket outlets.

questions.prompt: To meet the requirements of BS 7671, all overcurrent protective devices, without back-up protection on the supply side, must be capable of:

options.A: Not operating during a short-circuit fault
options.B: Operating at a current lower that their rated current
options.D: Withstanding the prospective short-circuit current at that point in the installation

questions.explanation: Every protective device must have a breaking capacity at least equal to the prospective fault current at its point of installation, unless backed up by another device. Otherwise it could fail to clear a fault safely and may rupture, causing fire or injury.

A.text: Failure to operate on short circuit would leave destructive fault energy flowing, which is the opposite of the protective device's function.

B.text: Operating below rated current would cause nuisance trips during legitimate load and does not describe the required short-circuit withstand capability.

C.text: A device should carry rated current without operating; tripping exactly at In is not the breaking-capacity requirement being assessed.

D.text: Every protective device must have a breaking capacity at least equal to the prospective fault current at its point of installation, unless backed up by another device. Otherwise it could fail to clear a fault safely and may rupture, causing fire or injury.

questions.prompt: Which is a method of fault protection
questions.explanation: Fault protection guards against contact with parts that become live under a first fault, and reinforced insulation provides this by a single insulation system equivalent to double insulation. Insulation of live parts, obstacles and placing out of reach are basic protection measures instead.

A.text: Insulation of live parts prevents normal contact and is basic protection, not the insulation arrangement intended to remain safe after one layer fails.

B.text: Obstacles deter accidental approach in controlled locations but do not protect exposed metalwork after an insulation fault.

C.text: Placing live parts out of reach is another restricted basic-protection method and does not provide a second insulation barrier.

D.text: Fault protection guards against contact with parts that become live under a first fault, and reinforced insulation provides this by a single insulation system equivalent to double insulation. Insulation of live parts, obstacles and placing out of reach are basic protection measures instead.

questions.prompt: An undervoltage device has operated and restoring the supply may cause danger. The reclosure of this device should be

options.A: Automatic when under the supervision of a competent person
options.D: Possible only with the use of a key or tool

questions.explanation: Where restoring supply after an undervoltage operation could create danger, such as machinery restarting unexpectedly, automatic reclosure must be prevented. Manual operation ensures a person deliberately re-energises the circuit only when it is safe to do so.

A.text: Supervision cannot make an unexpected automatic restart safe when someone may still be in contact with the machinery at restoration.

B.text: A time delay merely postpones the same uncommanded restart and cannot confirm that guards, tools and people are clear.

C.text: Where restoring supply after an undervoltage operation could create danger, such as machinery restarting unexpectedly, automatic reclosure must be prevented. Manual operation ensures a person deliberately re-energises the circuit only when it is safe to do so.

D.text: A key may be one control method, but the essential requirement is deliberate manual reclosure rather than a universal keyed mechanism.

questions.prompt: A SELV source can be derived from which one of the following?
questions.explanation: A SELV system relies on electrical separation between the source and the supply mains so a fault cannot raise the low-voltage circuit to a dangerous potential. A safety isolating transformer provides that segregated double-wound construction; an autotransformer shares a common winding and cannot guarantee separation.

A.text: An autotransformer shares a winding and conductive connection with the mains, so a primary fault can transfer dangerous voltage to the ELV side.

B.text: A generic double-wound transformer is not necessarily built and verified to the safety-isolating requirements needed for a SELV source.

C.text: A SELV system relies on electrical separation between the source and the supply mains so a fault cannot raise the low-voltage circuit to a dangerous potential. A safety isolating transformer provides that segregated double-wound construction; an autotransformer shares a common winding and cannot guarantee separation.

D.text: A step-up transformer raises voltage and its name gives no assurance of the protective separation and low output needed for SELV.

questions.prompt: Except where otherwise recommended by the manufacturer, spotlights and projectors rated at over 100 W and up to 300 W shall be installed at a minimum distance from combustible materials of
questions.explanation: Luminaires emit significant radiant heat that can ignite nearby materials, so minimum spacing increases with lamp rating. questions.prompt: Where particular risks of fire exist, the classification for high density occupation areas with easy conditions of evacuation is
questions.explanation: Conditions of evacuation are graded by occupant density and how readily people can leave. The BD classification combining high density with easy evacuation conditions is BD3, which reflects areas crowded with people but where exit routes remain straightforward to use.

questions.prompt: Which of the following under certain conditions could be used as an earth electrode?

options.B: A purpose-made earth rod installed for the electrical installation

questions.explanation: A purpose-made rod is a controlled, durable connection to the general mass of Earth. Gas pipes and public or private water-service pipes must not be relied on as electrodes because they may be altered, removed or replaced with plastic and could introduce dangerous current into a utility service.

B.text: A purpose-made rod is a controlled, durable connection to the general mass of Earth. Gas pipes and public or private water-service pipes must not be relied on as electrodes because they may be altered, removed or replaced with plastic and could introduce dangerous current into a utility service.

C.text: An insulated water pipe has no reliable conductive contact with the general mass of Earth and therefore cannot function as an electrode.

D.text: Public water pipework is outside the installer's control and is increasingly replaced by plastic, so its continuity cannot be relied upon.

questions.prompt: The value of the external loop impedance can be found by more than one method. One of these could be taking a reading at

options.A: Both at the supply and at the furthest outlet, and subtracting one result from the other
options.B: The furthest outlet from the origin of the supply

questions.explanation: The external loop impedance Ze represents only the supply side back to the transformer, so it must be measured with the installation disconnected. Taking the reading at the origin of supply, with the consumer's main earth disconnected, captures that external path without including the installation's own conductors.

Taking the reading at the origin of supply, with the consumer's main earth disconnected, captures that external path without including the installation's own conductors.

questions.prompt: Undervoltage protection circuit are required to stay de-energised where the restoration of power may cause

options.C: Unexpected stopping of the motor circuit

questions.prompt: An electric fire having an element exposed to touch would increase the risk of an electric shock by
questions.explanation: Basic protection guards against contact with parts that are live in normal service, such as an exposed heating element. An element open to touch defeats that basic protection, so the increased shock risk arises through basic contact with a normally live part.

questions.prompt: Which of the following energy sources is not suitable for a SELV supply?
questions.explanation: A SELV supply must be electrically separated from higher-voltage circuits so no fault can transfer a dangerous voltage. questions.prompt: A PEN Conductor must

options.A: Have a switching or isolating device
options.C: Not have a switching or isolating device

questions.prompt: SPD Stands for

questions.prompt: Which listed load arrangement most clearly calls for a three-phase industrial distribution board?
questions.explanation: Four three-phase motors create several balanced three-phase industrial loads, so a three-phase board is the natural distribution arrangement. questions.prompt: Which listed wiring method can protect a cable concealed less than 50 mm deep in a wall outside the prescribed zones?

options.A: Be enclosed in earthed metallic conduit

A.text: Earthed metallic conduit is one accepted method because it gives mechanical protection and provides a fault path if a fixing penetrates the wiring. Unearthed conduit does not provide that fault path, a 500 mA RCD is not additional protection, and the cable is not absolutely prohibited where a compliant protective method is used.

questions.prompt: The minimum information contained on a periodic inspection and testing notice would be the

options.B: Date of inspection and inspectors name
